request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Admission Date: November 2013
Discharge Date: January 2017
Length of Stay: 3 years and 2 months
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The 52-year-old male patient was diagnosed with a left temporal GBM in November 2013 after he presented with memory deficits and aphasia. He underwent standard radiation and temozolomide treatment initially. At the time of ketogenic diet therapy, the patient was on fifth-line treatment for recurrent GBM, which included the FDA-approved antiangiogenic therapy bevacizumab and irinotecan. Due to nausea, headaches, and fatigue, the patient started a ketogenic diet for 3.5 months. During the diet period, the patient was able to add physical exercise to his routine along with dance lessons. After discontinuation of the diet, the patient reported worsening symptoms, including difficulty reading and decreased short term memory. The patient's symptoms continued to progress, and he passed away in January 2017.

Clinical Findings:
During the hospital course, the patient reported memory deficits and aphasia. The initial treatment included standard radiation and temozolomide, followed by the antiangiogenic therapy bevacizumab and irinotecan. The patient was then switched to a ketogenic diet for 3.5 months, which resulted in increased physical activity, but also cravings for carbs and sweets. The patient's symptoms worsened after discontinuation of the diet, and his disease continued to progress until his death in January 2017.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient passed away due to the progression of his left temporal GBM.

Follow-Up:
The patient passed away in January 2017, and no further follow-up was possible.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
Glioblastoma of the left temporal lobe is a malignant neoplasm of the brain. In ICD-10-AM, malignant neoplasm of the brain is C71, and the temporal lobe is C71.2. The three-character category is therefore C71.

CODE: C71
